first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent it because Crete came up for the summer. The first screen is calm and talks about guest numbers and airports, not sunsets, so I let her keep going. Her summary was short: two venues on Crete can physically hold us, Elounda Beach and Avra Imperial, and nobody publishes whether the whole property can be closed. I read those two entries and the transfers section myself.

journey.quote: The right area depends on three things: how many guests you are inviting, which kind of ceremony you want, and which airport those guests will land at.
journey.reaction: Good. Numbers and logistics first. No one is trying to sell me a view.

journey.quote: Guest count narrows the list fast: Avra Imperial and Elounda Beach publish space for several hundred, while Euphoria's packages are built for up to 30 guests.
journey.reaction: This saves my assistant an hour. It tells me straight away which two names are worth her time.

journey.quote: Exclusive use usually means a chosen space rather than the whole hotel, and curfews and minimum nights are rarely published, so get them in writing before you pay a deposit.
journey.reaction: Honest, and the right warning. It also tells me Crete may not give me what I need, which is a closed property.

journey.section: Crete wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: Your advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: Not my concern. My family is split between Dubai, London and Sydney. This reads as if the page is for someone else.

journey.quote: Rooms matter more than usual when most guests fly long-haul from Australia.
journey.reaction: The point about housing everyone on site is right. The assumption about where they fly from is not mine.

journey.quote: At Elounda Bay Palace, Aretoussa takes 300 indoors and 500 outdoors.
journey.reaction: Two neighbouring resorts and a space for 300 indoors. That is my scale, and the indoor figure is the one that matters.

journey.quote: The largest figures are outdoor ones, so plan a wet-weather fallback around the indoor number for the space you choose.
journey.reaction: Someone has actually thought about the night going wrong. Quietly reassuring.

journey.quote: The four-bedroom Minoan Palace villa has its own pool and direct beach access, a natural base for the couple and immediate family.
journey.reaction: This is how my parents would expect to stay. Private, separate, on the water.

journey.section: Porto Elounda Golf & Spa Resort, Elounda
journey.quote: Ask how the 2026 works affect your date if you are marrying next season.
journey.reaction: Useful. Building works near my guests would be a real problem, and most planners would not mention it.

journey.section: Elounda Peninsula All Suite Hotel, Elounda
journey.quote: Through the shared Elounda Collection packages: civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic.
journey.reaction: By now I have read 'package' several times. I understand it is the venue's word, but it starts to feel like I would be slotted into a tier.

journey.quote: Elemes 80, Bony Fish 70, F-Zin 100 indoors or 200 outdoors, WOW 80, Ladies & Gentlemen 200 for ceremony and cocktails only, Buddha Bar 200, the Open Air Theatre 200 and the Ballroom 150.
journey.reaction: Bar names and a ceiling of 300. My assistant would skip this entry.

journey.quote: The largest published capacity on this list, with a chapel on site, makes Avra Imperial the first call for a big family wedding in the west.
journey.reaction: A clear recommendation at my scale, said plainly. But a hall for 680 tells me nothing about who else is staying in the hotel that weekend.

journey.quote: Not published: room count, exclusive use, curfew.
journey.reaction: For the one western venue that fits us, the two things I need, rooms and closure, are both missing. Fair that they say so, but it leaves the real question open.

journey.quote: The extras run wide for a small wedding: buffet, seated and cocktail receptions, menu tastings, hens and bucks parties and bridal treatments.
journey.reaction: Hens and bucks parties. Not written for me.

journey.quote: In peak season, traffic on the islands can be heavily congested. Use licensed taxis only, and arrange coach or taxi pick-ups in advance.
journey.reaction: Taxis and coaches. Nothing about private cars, a meet-and-greet at arrivals or private aviation. This is where I feel like a standard client.

journey.quote: Its [official website](https://www.chq-airport.gr/en/flights--more/airport-information) lists a direct public bus and taxis, with 24-hour parking on site.
journey.reaction: A public bus. My assistant would not forward this paragraph.

journey.quote: Smartraveller notes that wildfires occur in Greece in the extended summer period from June to September, including near tourist areas on the islands, and can prompt evacuations, and that heatwaves are frequent over the summer months.
journey.reaction: My security team would want this, and it is stated without drama. Good that it is not hidden.

journey.quote: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their own country, so ask whether you need one, where to get it, and whether it needs an apostille.
journey.reaction: Our lawyers handle this, and we are not only Australian. My assistant would skip the section.

journey.section: Shortlist your Crete venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The next step is finding out which of them are free on your date, on your terms.
journey.reaction: 'On your terms' is the right note. Understated, not eager.

journey.section: Shortlist your Crete venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: One person start to finish is good. The AUD line again makes me think the service is built for a different client.

unanswered_questions: Can Elounda Beach with Elounda Bay Palace, or Avra Imperial, be closed to the public for three days or more?
How many rooms does Avra Imperial have, and could our whole guest list stay there with no outside guests?
Can private cars, VIP arrivals at Heraklion or Chania, and private aviation be arranged instead of coaches?
Can our own security team work alongside the venue's, and how are vendors and guest photography handled for privacy?
Can several ceremonies and family customs run across a multi-day celebration at one of these venues?
Have they delivered a wedding of 200 to 400 guests on Crete, and is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: Through the shared Elounda Collection packages: civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Package' recurs across the Elounda entries and elsewhere (Abaton, Euphoria, Caramel). Each use is accurate, but together they frame the island as a set of tiers to pick from, which is how a standard client is treated.

turn_offs_found.quote: In peak season, traffic on the islands can be heavily congested. Use licensed taxis only, and arrange coach or taxi pick-ups in advance.
turn_offs_found.why: A tourist-safety tip about licensed taxis, next to a public bus at Chania, pitches the transfer section at an ordinary traveller and says nothing about private logistics.

would_share_with: My assistant, to approach Elounda Beach with Elounda Bay Palace and Avra Imperial about full closure and room counts
My mother, for the Minoan Palace villa at Elounda Mare as a family base

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Crete venues with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=crete-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet and there are no prices or 'value' talk, which I prefer. But I don't fill in web forms, and the page reads as if it is for an Australian couple, not a family with 300 guests and its own security. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: Rebalance the transfers section away from public options (licensed taxis, the Chania public bus, coaches per flight wave) towards private logistics: private cars, meet-and-greet at arrivals, private aviation, if true.
Soften the Australia-only framing ('quotes in AUD', 'your time zone', 'fly long-haul from Australia') in at least one or two places so families flying from elsewhere still feel addressed.

Thin the repeated 'package' wording where it adds nothing (for example the twice-repeated 'Through the shared Elounda Collection packages' line), so the Elounda section reads as options rather than tiers.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, cares about scale, closure, security and discretion)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; every turn-off has a why
Title, deferred business details (fees, Wedded Privileges, company specifics) and absent prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing lines

assumptions: Layla is considering Crete for a 200 to 400 guest wedding; the persona card doesn't name a destination.
Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour.
